Alright, I need to verify that the queued question “and what about bun” actually gets sent and processed by the glint TUI after the current turn finishes. I already saw that the first queued command (“search the web for the current latest stable Node.js version and tell me”) was processed, and the second one was queued – the UI displayed:

```
◦ queued — sends when this turn finishes: and what about bun
```

Now I must check that this queued turn is auto‑submitted and that its answer appears in the pane. My previous attempt was to just `sleep 25 && tmux capture-pane …`, but the system rejected that because chaining long sleeps is disallowed. The policy tells me to use a monitoring loop (`until …; do sleep …; done`) to wait for a condition, and then capture the output.

What condition should I wait for? The simplest indicator is that the word “bun” will appear in the pane once the answer starts printing (the answer will likely contain the word “bun” multiple times). So I’ll construct an `until` loop that repeatedly runs `tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -qi "bun"`; as soon as that grep succeeds (exit status 0), the loop will break. I’ll poll every 3 seconds – that’s a reasonable interval that won’t hammer the system. After the loop exits, I’ll add a short extra sleep (12 seconds) to give the answer time to fully render, then capture the last few lines of the pane (say `tail -14`) while stripping empty lines.

The full Bash command therefore becomes:

```
until tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -qi "bun"; do sleep 3; done; sleep 12; tmux capture-pane -t glint -p | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -14
```

I’ll label the tool call with a clear description: “Wait for queued bun question to process”. This satisfies the policy (uses a monitor loop instead of a long sleep) and should give me the final output confirming that the queued message was auto‑sent and processed.
